Hide 3 Crown Jewels and 3 Sensors, one token in each Prod app (F, G, H, J, K, L). The Attacker can see where your tokens are, but not what they are.

Tap a Prod cell to move that app’s token there. Tap a token to switch it between Jewel and Sensor.

    Settings

    Add ?seed=abc to the URL to replay the same random setup and AI rolls.

    Playtest prototype. vDefend is a trademark of Broadcom. Rules: docs/RINGFENCE-GAME-DESIGN.md.

    How to play

    You are the Defender. The AI is the Attacker. Each round you take 3 actions, then the Attacker takes 3.

    • You win at the end of your turn with a Segmentation Score of 10, or if round 12 ends.
    • The Attacker wins by exfiltrating 2 Crown Jewels.

    Business flows are hidden

    Each game, apps talk to each other over hidden business flows. Security Intelligence reveals them as traffic history builds up: everyday flows from round 2, month-end flows in round 4. Month-end flows first run in round 5.

    If your policy blocks a real flow while it runs, that’s an outage: −2 score, and an emergency allow rule opens the edge again, for the Attacker too.

    Your actions: DFW 1-2-3-4, plus SSP

    • 1 Assess: +2 Insight. Insight pays for everything else. Stage 1: Segmentation Assessment.
    • 2 Harden an infrastructure service (NTP, DNS, LDAP) for 1 Insight. It evicts any stone there, closes the hub shortcut, and is no longer an exit. +1 score. Stage 2: Infrastructure Services.
    • 3 Segment: place up to 2 walls on border edges for 1 Insight. Seal the Dev/Prod boundary for +2 score and leakage alerts. Stage 3: Zones.
    • 4a Allow: publish the Security Intelligence recommendation for an app. This adds allow rules (exceptions) for every flow observed on its border. It’s free; manual exceptions cost 1 Insight each. Stage 4: recommendations.
    • 4b Ring-fence an app for Insight equal to its size. Everything on its border that isn’t an exception is blocked. +3 score. Afterwards you can also wall edges inside it. Stage 4: App microsegmentation.
    • ★ Deploy a face-down Sensor or Decoy on an empty cell for 1 Insight. SSP: IDS/IPS inspects the traffic you allow.

    The real workflow: observe traffic → publish exceptions for valid flows → lock down everything else. Skip a step and you break production, or leave paths open.

    The Attacker

    • Breach (once per turn): place a stone on row 1 or the internet-facing storefront H.
    • Spread: place a stone next to one of theirs across an open edge. Business flows are always open. Unhardened NTP, DNS and LDAP all connect to each other (the hub).
    • Recon: secretly look at a face-down token next to one of their stones.
    • Exfil: take a revealed Jewel whose stone is connected to an exit: row 1, storefront H, or unhardened infra.

    Tokens and capture

    • A stone that enters a Jewel reveals it. A Sensor removes the stone and ends the Attacker’s turn. A Decoy does nothing.
    • Quarantine: an attacker group with no open edge to an empty cell is removed. +1 score.

    Shortcuts: 1–6 pick an action · Esc cancel · U undo · E end turn.
